top_choice_rationale: P002 is a mature, cleanly attributed two-name award. The optical lattice clock rests on Katori's magic-wavelength trapping, which cancels the first-order light shift for many neutral atoms at once and so removes Doppler and recoil effects. Ye's group brought it to about 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, and several independent groups have reproduced and surpassed it. It is distinct from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize. P001 is a strong, broad and mature award and a close second: the Z2 topological insulator and the HgTe observation are a different class of matter from the 2016 prize, with a citation properly limited to the 2D quantum spin Hall state. Its cost is the visible omission of Hasan and of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang. I put P002 first on the achievement, while discounting my own field proximity, and I rank any award above P000 because both candidates are ripe.
recusal_note: Possible conflict from my profile: I had a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, and the lattice-clock candidate Jun Ye belongs to the Hall/JILA precision-spectroscopy community. I also work in atomic physics and laser spectroscopy at Lund. I know of no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye, and this simulation does not adjudicate recusals.
